publication.title: Design of a 65-kW Wireless Charging Station Characterized by Optimal Load Impedance Tracking Control
publication.journal: IEEE Open Journal of Vehicular Technology

application.description: Static EV wireless charging prototype; author describes compatibility with SAE J2954.

prototype.coupler_type: Double-D coil couplers with ferrite and magnetic/electric shielding
prototype.gap_definition: Vertical ground-assembly to vehicle-assembly coupling-element separation
prototype.misalignment_description: Back-to-back tests report misalignment up to 60% of coil dimensions; positioning study gives Delta X approximately +/-0.21 m and Delta Y approximately +/-0.14 m under a stated efficiency-above-91% envelope.
prototype.control_method: Active optimal load-impedance tracking with primary and secondary control; switching frequency tracks resonant frequency.
prototype.institution: University of West Bohemia (with University of Zilina co-authorship)

input_boundary.measurement_point: Author-labelled P_DC1 at primary-side DC link in the back-to-back configuration
excludes: Full 3-phase mains front end and complete battery/grid-recuperation chain

output_boundary.measurement_point: Author-labelled P_DC2 at the secondary-side DC link in the back-to-back configuration

efficiency.definition: Back-to-back system efficiency plotted between author-labelled P_DC1 and P_DC2; not full WCS mains-to-battery efficiency.

measurements.load_description: Back-to-back test using an externally excited DC generator as source; output/load condition per figure 18.
measurements.alignment_description: Authors state back-to-back tests include misalignment evaluation up to 60% of coil dimensions.
measurements.source_locator: Primary article, section V.B, pp.4-5, text immediately preceding/after Fig.18.
measurements.notes: Highest reported efficiency among the operational states described in this back-to-back test section; input voltage limit constrained power to approximately 58 kW.

input_boundary.measurement_point: Author-labelled P_DC1 at primary-side DC link in the back-to-back configuration
excludes: Full 3-phase mains front end and complete battery/grid-recuperation chain

output_boundary.measurement_point: Author-labelled P_DC2 at the secondary-side DC link in the back-to-back configuration

efficiency.definition: Back-to-back system efficiency plotted between author-labelled P_DC1 and P_DC2; not full WCS mains-to-battery efficiency.

measurements.load_description: Back-to-back test; authors state output exceeded nominal design power.
measurements.alignment_description: No specific misalignment value attached to this particular 20 cm point in the text.
measurements.source_locator: Primary article, section V.B, pp.4-5, text for Fig.19.
measurements.notes: Reported as >70 kW at 96.3%; the paper's nominal design rating is 65 kW. Keep actual test result distinct from nominal rating.

input_boundary.measurement_point: Author-labelled P_DC1 at primary-side DC link in the back-to-back configuration
excludes: Full 3-phase mains front end and complete battery/grid-recuperation chain

output_boundary.measurement_point: Author-labelled P_DC2 at the secondary-side DC link in the back-to-back configuration

efficiency.definition: Back-to-back system efficiency plotted between author-labelled P_DC1 and P_DC2; not full WCS mains-to-battery efficiency.

measurements.load_description: Back-to-back test using an externally excited DC generator as source.
measurements.alignment_description: No specific misalignment value attached to this particular 25 cm point in the text.
measurements.source_locator: Primary article, section V.B, pp.4-5, text for Fig.20.
measurements.notes: The paper describes this as the worst performance of the back-to-back operating cases.

input_boundary.measurement_point: Author-defined η_WCS whole charging-station input boundary; exact meter point / formula is not numerically enumerated in Table VII

output_boundary.measurement_point: Author-defined η_WCS whole charging-station output boundary through secondary-side power conversion to the battery / grid-recuperation load; exact meter point / formula is not numerically enumerated in Table VII

efficiency.definition: η_WCS, authors' whole wireless charging system efficiency in Table VII at 65 kW for the proposed third control strategy.

measurements.load_description: Full-power 65 kW control-strategy comparison; authors distinguish whole-chain η_WCS from η_DC-DC.
measurements.alignment_description: Nominal distance 20 cm for the reported control comparison context.
measurements.source_locator: Primary article, section V.C-V.D, pp.5-6, especially Table VII and adjacent definition of η_DC-DC / η_WCS.
measurements.notes: Table VII identifies the test as 65 kW and reports η_WCS=92.7%. The exact gap, frequency and power-in/output watt values are not stated for this comparison table; do not infer them from the adjacent 20 cm figure or set the input equal to nominal rating.

input_boundary.measurement_point: Output of primary-side DC-DC stage (input to the author's η_DC-DC subchain)

output_boundary.measurement_point: Output of secondary-side DC-DC stage (output of the author's η_DC-DC subchain)

efficiency.definition: η_DC-DC, authors' efficiency between primary and secondary DC-DC stages, including inverter, coupling elements and secondary rectifier; not full WCS efficiency.

measurements.load_description: Same Table VII full-power 65 kW control-strategy comparison.
measurements.alignment_description: Nominal distance 20 cm for the reported control comparison context.
measurements.source_locator: Primary article, section V.C-V.D, pp.5-6, lines introducing η_DC-DC and Table VII.
measurements.notes: Table VII identifies the control comparison as 65 kW and η_DC-DC=95.5%, but does not state measured input/output watt values, gap or frequency for that table row. This is the subchain metric, not η_WCS.

source_refs.locator: Sections V.A-V.D; Figs.16-25; Table VII; DOI 10.1109/OJVT.2025.3604561.
Appendix A, Table A1, IPT entry [52]; survey reports 70 kW, 96.3%, 83.5 kHz, 200 mm, West Bohemian University, EV, 2025.

lineage: One prototype / one publication with multiple distinct test modes and measurement boundaries; five measurements must not be counted as five independent prototype realizations.
limitations: Areas for transmitter and receiver couplers were not transcribed here because the cited sources' tabulated values were not identified in the accessible locator; missing values remain null.
Back-to-back test boundaries use author-labelled P_DC1/P_DC2 and are not the complete WCS/battery energy chain.
Authors state the grid-recuperation substitute in battery-load tests does not permit full-power testing.
Reported figures lack uncertainty intervals in the accessible text; no uncertainty is invented.
The 2026 survey is secondary for the 70 kW/96.3% summary; the 2025 paper is the primary source for the underlying operating point.

claim_audit.notes: Table VII at 65 kW reports 95.5% for eta_DC-DC (the subchain including inverter, couplers and secondary rectifier) and 92.7% for eta_WCS (whole wireless charging system). The abstract's 'overall system' wording appears to conflate or refer to a different operating condition; no reconciliation is invented.

publication.title: Smart design for next-gen wireless EV charging

application.description: Exposure-informed co-design of an 85 kHz Double-D EV charging pad.

prototype.coupler_type: Double-D coil with conductive/ferromagnetic shielding and rolled-edge shield concept
prototype.gap_definition: 20 cm transmitter-to-receiver coupling gap as stated for lab prototype efficiency
prototype.institution: University of West Bohemia; Czech Technical University in Prague; University of Zilina

input_boundary.measurement_point: Author-reported DC input boundary for DC-to-DC efficiency; exact meter plane not stated in abstract

output_boundary.measurement_point: Author-reported DC output boundary for DC-to-DC efficiency; exact meter plane not stated in abstract

efficiency.definition: DC-to-DC efficiency above 96% for the laboratory prototype at 20 cm; detailed meter boundary requires full-paper review.

measurements.notes: Measured prototype efficiency. The abstract does not specify output power, power boundary details, or uncertainty; these remain unreported.

engineering_metrics.name: Shielding loss reduction relative to reference geometry
engineering_metrics.source_locator: Abstract; FEM / surrogate multi-objective co-design description.
engineering_metrics.notes: Approximately 56% lower shielding loss; this is a design/model result, not an isolated direct measurement.

engineering_metrics.name: Mutual inductance range across reference and optimized geometry
engineering_metrics.notes: Reported as approximately 27.2–27.3 μH while reducing shielding losses.

source_refs.locator: Abstract; co-design method and prototype performance statement.

lineage: Separate 2026 exposure-informed DD pad prototype; shares authors/research lineage with Zavrel 2025 65 kW WCS, but exact physical prototype reuse is not established. Do not deduplicate automatically.
limitations: No nominal/output power or rated system capacity is given in the abstract.
Exact input/output meter locations for DC-to-DC efficiency and uncertainty are not given in the abstract.
Shielding-loss reduction and mutual inductance are model/co-design metrics; not measured load power.
Magnetic-field profiles are reported measured and consistent with simulation, but numeric field values are not transcribed here.
Electric-field exposure is assessed in simulation using a rolled-edge shield concept; do not label it a physical measurement.

publication.title: Receiver, Vehicle, and Roadway Systems for a Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer Roadway Testbed
publication.journal: Purdue Joint Transportation Research Program / FHWA technical report

application.description: Dynamic roadway transfer into a retrofitted Class-8 electric truck on an instrumented public-road testbed.

prototype.coupler_type: Road-embedded transmitter coil array with vehicle-mounted receiver
prototype.gap_definition: Not reported in the abstract; roadway coils embedded 2.4 inches below pavement surface.
prototype.misalignment_description: Abstract reports strong misalignment tolerance and reliable high-power delivery without active vehicle-roadway alignment; quantitative offset envelope not in abstract.
prototype.institution: Purdue University; Indiana Department of Transportation testbed

output_boundary.measurement_point: Power delivered by road-to-vehicle DWPT system; exact meter plane not specified in abstract

efficiency.definition: Efficiency approaching 85% as reported in report abstract; exact source/output energy boundary and operating point not specified in abstract.

measurements.alignment_description: Dynamic operation with vehicle motion; abstract reports strong misalignment tolerance.
measurements.notes: Abstract reports 50–190 kW at speeds up to 65 mph. Do not interpret this range as constant power across all speeds, or assume efficiency applies uniformly to the entire power range.

engineering_metrics.name: Transmitter coil embed depth below pavement surface
engineering_metrics.notes: Coils embedded 2.4 in beneath existing rigid pavement.

engineering_metrics.name: Maximum reported vehicle speed during operation
engineering_metrics.notes: Speed at which high-power dynamic transfer is reported; do not interpret as a full-speed performance curve.

limitations: Abstract gives no transfer gap, frequency, explicit power meter boundary, uncertainty, duty cycle or run-duration details.
Efficiency approaching 85% is not defined to the same measurement boundary as the 65 kW static EV IPT measurements.
Power range and maximum vehicle speed are abstract-level summaries and must not be combined into a single operating point.
Human exposure result in abstract states magnetic flux densities well below exposure limits, but numeric field values and test paths need report-level extraction.

publication.title: Findings from Japan's First Public Road Experiments of Dynamic Wireless Power Transfer to Electric Vehicle

application.description: Public-road dynamic wireless power transfer to a moving electric vehicle.

prototype.coupler_type: Road-embedded transmitter and vehicle receiver coils
prototype.misalignment_description: Public road vehicle operation; quantitative offset tolerance not stated in abstract.
prototype.institution: Nagaoka University of Technology; Tokyo Electric Power Company Holdings; TEPCO Power Grid

output_boundary.measurement_point: Power delivered to moving EV; exact meter location not stated in abstract

efficiency.definition: Not stated in abstract. The reported 63.3% is an energy-replenishment share, not transfer efficiency.

measurements.load_description: Actual electric vehicle driven on public road.
measurements.alignment_description: Dynamic road trial; exact alignment tolerances not stated in abstract.
measurements.source_locator: Abstract, IEEJ Transactions on Industry Applications 146(4), DOI 10.1541/ieejias.146.194.
measurements.notes: Approximately 10 kW delivered while moving; authors report recharging 63.3% of the power consumed in driving.

engineering_metrics.name: Fraction of driving-consumption quantity replenished by DWPT (authors' reported metric)
engineering_metrics.notes: The abstract states that approximately 63.3% of the power consumed in driving was recharged by DWPT. This is a vehicle-level replenishment ratio, not a wireless-link conversion efficiency. Exact numerator/denominator integration interval and measurement boundary require full-paper extraction.

engineering_metrics.name: Public-road field operation duration
engineering_metrics.notes: Authors report 18 months of field testing and stable underground transmitter parameters.

source_refs.locator: Abstract; IEEJ Transactions on Industry Applications 146(4), article page 194.

limitations: Abstract does not report efficiency, operating frequency, gap, power boundary, vehicle speed or uncertainty.
The 63.3% drive-energy replenishment metric is not WPT energy-transfer efficiency.
18 months refers to reported public-road field testing; no detailed failure-rate denominator or uptime percentage is available from the abstract.
